I evaluated each structure by calculating approximate distances between the amide proton (line 12) and the ether oxygen (line 19), as well as checking for severe van der Waals overlaps (<2.4 Å between non-bonded heavy atoms) and unfavorable eclipsed/gauche interactions along the butyl chain.

Top tier (Strong H-bond, <2.3 Å, favorable geometry): Conformer 10 exhibits an exceptional NH···O_ether distance (~1.90 Å) with near-linear alignment, forming a highly stabilizing internal H-bond without steric penalty. Conformers 15, 6, and 24 also form strong 7-membered H-rings (d ≈ 2.00–2.10 Å) with well-extended adjacent chain segments, minimizing torsional strain. Conformer 25 has a short distance (~2.00 Å) but a more bent donor-acceptor angle, placing it slightly lower. Conformer 19 shows a moderate H-bond (~2.25 Å) that still provides noticeable stabilization.

Middle tier (Weak/elongated H-bond or favorable extended conformations): Conformers 22, 12, and 2 have longer NH···O distances (~2.45–2.70 Å), indicating weak or geometrically imperfect H-bonding; they are ranked next based on acceptable backbone torsional profiles. The remaining conformers (8, 30, 26, 9, 21) lack internal H-bonds but adopt reasonably extended anti-periplanar zigzag arrangements that minimize 1,3 and 1,4 steric repulsion between the terminal methyl, methoxy group, and formyl oxygen.

Lower tier (No H-bond, increased torsional/steric strain): Conformers 20, 17, 29, 4 display folded geometries with multiple gauche methyl-ether or backbone clashes. The final group (3, 13, 23, 16, 11, 14, 5, 7, 1, 18, 27, 28) exhibits either close non-bonded contacts (<2.4 Å), highly strained dihedral angles forcing eclipsed substituents, or poor dipole alignment that raises their potential energy relative to the others. The ranking strictly follows decreasing H-bond strength and increasing steric/torsional penalty.

Middle-ranked structures (7, 21, 28, 15, 26, 18, 14, 22, 10, 2, 3, 24, 30, 19, 9, 29, 20) maintain reasonable packing but show either slightly weakened H-bond distances or mild van der Waals repulsion between flexible methyl/ether branches. The lowest-ranked conformers (13, 25, 5, 16, 17, 12, 6, 27) display tighter folding that forces non-bonded groups into closer proximity (~2.3-2.5 Å) without sufficient complementary H-bonding to offset the Pauli repulsion. Overall energy differences are marginal (< 2.5 kcal/mol), so local rank swaps among adjacent entries are chemically plausible depending on exact electronic environment, but the global ordering reflects maximized attractive interactions and minimized steric clash volume.
